title: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (PALM-COEIN)
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (FIGO 2023)
FIGO AUB System 1 & 2 (PALM-COEIN); ACOG guidance on acute AUB in non-pregnant reproductive-age women

changelog.change: Initial entry — PALM-COEIN classification, acute and maintenance medical treatment, and endometrial-biopsy indications.

summary: First rule out pregnancy. Classify by PALM-COEIN (structural vs non-structural). Acute heavy bleeding is managed medically first — high-dose oestrogen or progestin, or IV conjugated oestrogen if the endometrium is atrophic — then transitioned to maintenance, with the LNG-IUD the best-evidence long-term option.

rows: Combined OCP 3×/day ×7 days; OR high-dose progestin; OR conjugated oestrogen 25 mg IV q4–6h (if atrophic)
Then transition to maintenance. Tranexamic acid is a useful adjunct
LNG-IUD (Mirena) — best evidence; combined OCP; progestin-only pill; cyclic progestin 10 mg on days 16–25
GnRH agonist as a short-term pre-operative bridge for fibroids
Age ≥ 45 with AUB; any age with hyperplasia risk factors; persistent AUB despite treatment

body.text: Haemodynamically unstable bleeding: resuscitate, correct coagulopathy, and involve GYN — options include IV oestrogen, intrauterine tamponade (balloon), uterine artery embolisation, or D&C. Always check a β-hCG first.
